1: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and grease 12 muffin cups.
2: Mix the banana, egg, milk and oil.
3: Fold in the flour, oats, baking powder and cinnamon without overmixing.
4: Divide into the cups and bake for 20 to 22 minutes.
5: Whisk the eggs with the milk and oil.
6: Fold in the flour and baking powder until smooth.
7: Cook over medium heat, about 2 minutes per side.
8: Serve in finger-width strips for the youngest children.
9: Coarsely mash the lentils with a fork.
10: Mix with the grated carrot, egg, breadcrumbs and garlic.
11: Shape into flat, firmly packed patties.
12: Brown for 3 to 4 minutes per side in the oil.
13: Cook the sweet potato and chicken in the broth until tender.
14: Purée with the cooking liquid and the oil.
15: Adjust the texture to the child's age: smooth, mashed or in pieces.
16: Bring the milk to a simmer with the grated apple.
17: Add the oats and cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
18: Let cool slightly — the texture thickens as it cools.
19: Blend the dates into a paste in a food processor.
20: Add the peanut butter, oats, chia and vanilla, then pulse.
21: Roll into small balls and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
22: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil, then add the diced chicken.
23: Add the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
24: Stir in the cream off the heat.
25: Toss with the cooked pasta, cut short for young children.
26: Finely chop the raw fish and the onion.
27: Mix with the egg and half the breadcrumbs.
28: Shape into nuggets and roll them in the remaining breadcrumbs.
29: Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes, turning halfway through.
30: Rinse the chickpeas in warm water.
31: Blend all the ingredients until very smooth.
32: Loosen with water as needed — smoother for younger children.
34: Beat the melted butter, sugar, eggs and vanilla.
35: Fold in the bananas, then the dry ingredients.
36: Bake in a loaf pan for 55 to 60 minutes.
37: Cream the butter and sugar, then add the egg.
38: Fold in the dry ingredients, then the raisins.
39: Drop flattened balls onto a baking sheet.
41: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and oil 8 muffin cups.
42: Whisk the eggs with the milk.
43: Add the drained vegetables and the cheese.
44: Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the centre is set.
45: Soften the onion in the oil.
46: Add the cubed squash and the broth, then simmer for 20 minutes.
47: Blend with the coconut milk until velvety.
48: Cook the pasta and set aside.
49: Make a roux with the butter and flour, then pour in the milk.
50: Stir in the squash purée and the cheese off the heat.
52: Mix all the ingredients without overworking the meat.
53: Shape into meatballs the size of a ping-pong ball.
55: Mash or quarter them for younger children.
56: Cook the rice in the milk over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring often.
57: Add the maple syrup and vanilla at the end of cooking.
59: Blend all the ingredients until smooth.
60: Serve with a spoon or in a sippy cup, depending on age.
61: Gently warm the peanut butter, honey and oil.
62: Pour over the oats, raisins and nuts, then mix well.
63: Press firmly into a parchment-lined pan.
64: Bake at 160 °C for 20 minutes, then cool completely before cutting.
65: Whisk the chia, milk, syrup and vanilla.
66: Refrigerate for 4 hours, whisking once after 30 minutes.
67: Top with blueberries just before serving.
68: Squeeze the grated cucumber dry in a clean cloth.
69: Stir into the yogurt with the lemon and garlic.
70: Serve with vegetables prepared to suit the child's age.
71: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil.
72: Add the diced chicken and brown it.
73: Pour in the broth, add the carrot and simmer for 15 minutes.
74: Stir in the couscous, cover and let it swell for 5 minutes.
75: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil until translucent.
76: Add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then add the broth one ladle at a time, stirring.
77: In the last 5 minutes, add the peas and the shrimp.
78: Remove from the heat and stir in the parmesan.
79: Mix the oats, flaxseed and cinnamon.
80: Pour in the maple syrup and oil, then coat well.
81: Spread on a baking sheet and bake at 150 °C for 20 minutes, stirring halfway.
82: Fold in the apricots once cooled.
83: Spread the chicken, cheese and bell pepper over half of each tortilla.
84: Fold over and brown in a pan, 2 to 3 minutes per side.
85: Let cool slightly, then cut into narrow wedges.
86: Soften the onion and carrot in the oil for 5 minutes.
87: Add the tomatoes, broth and basil, then bring to a boil.
88: Add the pasta and cook according to the package.
89: Mash a few vegetables with a fork to thicken.
90: Pat the tofu dry and cube it, then coat in cornstarch.
91: Brown the cubes in the oil on all sides.
92: Mix the soy sauce, syrup, garlic and ginger, pour over and let it coat for 1 minute.
94: Mix the eggs, applesauce, oil and syrup.
95: Fold in the flour, baking powder and cinnamon, then the carrots.
96: Bake in muffin cups for 18 to 20 minutes.
97: Cook the pasta according to the package.
98: Sear the salmon in the oil, then flake it with a fork.
99: Warm the cream with the garlic, then toss with the pasta, salmon and parmesan.
100: Cut the pasta short for the youngest children.
101: Blend all the ingredients until smooth.
102: Cook small pancakes over medium heat, 2 minutes per side.
104: Scramble the eggs in the oil, then set aside.
105: Stir-fry the carrot and peas for 3 minutes.
106: Add the rice and soy sauce, return the eggs and heat through.
107: Rinse the rice in cold water, then drain it.
108: Pour the coconut milk and water into a saucepan, add the rice and cook over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often.
109: Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
110: Purée the mango until smooth and spoon it over the warm pudding.
111: Serve warm. Before 9 months, blend everything for a perfectly smooth texture.
112: Peel the apples, core them and cut into cubes.
114: Put the apples, dates and water in a saucepan, cover and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes.
115: Add the cinnamon and lemon juice, then purée until very smooth.
116: Serve warm or cold. Before 9 months, pass the sauce through a sieve.
117: Cut the butternut squash and the carrot into cubes.
118: Pour the broth into a saucepan, add the squash and carrot, then simmer covered for 20 minutes.
119: Add the lentils and olive oil, then continue for 5 minutes.
120: Purée until smooth using the cooking liquid.
121: Adjust the texture to the child's age: smooth at 6 months, mashed around 9 months.
122: Peel the sweet potato and cut it into cubes.
123: Pour the broth into a saucepan, add the chicken pieces and the sweet potato, then cook over medium heat for 15 minutes.
124: Add the peas and continue cooking for 5 minutes.
125: Check that the chicken is cooked through, then add the canola oil.
126: Purée or mash with a fork, depending on the child's age.
128: Peel the sweet potato and cut it into thick sticks, about the width of an adult finger.
129: Coat with olive oil and sprinkle with cinnamon.
130: Bake for 25 minutes, until a stick crushes between two fingers.
131: Let cool slightly before serving. A stick should give under light pressure.
132: Mash the banana with a fork.
133: Mix the rolled oats, banana, applesauce and cinnamon.
134: Let rest for 5 minutes so the oats absorb the moisture.
135: Shape into flat patties and brown them in canola oil in a pan, 3 minutes per side.
136: Let cool slightly. Cut into strips for a child aged 6 to 8 months.
137: Bring the oat beverage to a simmer in a saucepan.
138: Add the rolled oats and chia seeds, then cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
139: Purée the mango and stir it in off the heat with the cinnamon.
140: Let cool slightly — the oatmeal thickens as it cools.
141: Blend before 9 months for a smooth texture.
142: Mix the ground flaxseed with 60 ml of oat beverage and let rest for 5 minutes.
143: Whisk the rice flour, the remaining oat beverage and the applesauce.
144: Stir in the flax mixture until the batter is smooth.
145: Cook in a pan with canola oil, 2 minutes per side.
